thread:
Rita Gomez: heads-up: we're sketching an authn handshake for service-to-service calls that avoids sending full role graphs. want quick feedback on the shim.
Anton Vasile: curious — do you mean a one-time exchange that yields a short-lived claim + registry id?
Rita Gomez: exactly. flow: caller presents API key (legacy or new), broker issues ephemeral JWT with fields: sub, rid, bv, exp. gateway checks signature + local cache for rid -> ACL.
Jayden Park: sounds sensible. question: how do we handle parameterized permissions (e.g., dataset:id)?
Rita Gomez: include a scoped claim like ds:hash in the token. gateway does simple match against role predicates loaded from bundle. avoids blowing up token size.
Anton Vasile: migration ops: for hosted long-lived keys, broker should mint ephemeral token without requiring customer rotation. log mapping and mark legacy key for deprecation.
Rita Gomez: yes. we'll also emit an audit event every exchange. infra-bot: added checklist item "broker-ephemeral-audit" to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/authn-shim
Jayden Park: perf: gateway hot path must avoid per-request remote authz. propose session cache for verified tokens and bundle cache for rid lookups. verify signature on new tokens only.
Rita Gomez: agreed. next steps: Anton prototype broker adapter, Jayden bench session/cache parameters, I'll write a short RFC appendix with examples and failure modes. sync Friday 11am?
Anton Vasile: Friday 11 works. will have a tiny prototype.
Jayden Park: will bench and aim for <8ms overhead on happy path.
Rita Gomez: thanks, team. we'll capture tradeoffs (latency vs freshness vs audit) in the RFC appendix.
